description: Code, plans with fingerprints, derived data, extracted GEFS and ERA5 footprint series and full results for a chronological test of whether conformal 90% prediction intervals for day-ahead electricity load, calibrated on earlier winters, remain calibrated in the next extreme-cold event. 38 weather-defined events in PJM, MISO, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO and ISO-NE (2014-2026) and two base forecasts (a gradient-boosting quantile forecaster and the operators' EIA-930 day-ahead demand forecasts). Across 38 events, conformalized intervals cover 0.64 of event hours against 0.84 of winter hours (gap 20.3 percentage points, cluster-robust 95% interval 10.0-30.5 over 15 cold outbreaks); intervals around the operators' forecasts show a gap of 18.2 points. All numbers in the accompanying manuscript are generated by the included scripts. Version 2.0.0 supersedes versions 1.0-1.2, whose headline claims came from an earlier design and from errors that were later corrected.
title: Calibrated for the Winter, Not for the Cold Snap: code and data for a chronological benchmark of 38 extreme-cold events in six U.S. power systems
